claims.assertion: RydeX is a fixed-quote service: the trip was charged $34.38 as a flat quoted fare (base $3.90 + distance $23.39 for 16.6 km + time $5.62 + platform $1.47), and the billed distance of 16.6 km equals the optimal route of 16.6 km, so no extra distance was ever billed to the rider.

The rider's demand to 'refund the extra distance' has no monetary basis: RD-2's refund formula only applies to metered RydeTAXI fares, and for a non-metered service such as RydeX the refundable amount for a distance complaint is zero, which maps to no_action.

The one off-route segment (09:06–09:13, 4.84 km added, up to 1176 m off the optimal route) generated no charge to the rider at all, since no unpublished surcharge, ERP/toll item or waiting fee appears on the bill and waiting was $0.00.

The rerouted segment is explained by a GPS re-route taken in dense traffic with no incidents: the optimal corridor's Ayer Rajah Expressway ran at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) and the Central Expressway at band 4 (30–39 km/h) throughout the trip window, and Ryde permits the driver to follow the GPS to the fastest or most efficient route.

There is no unrecovered detour to refund because the driver did not collect any excess metered amount — no surge was applied (1.0×) and the fare breakdown contains no manual or unpublished add-on items.

No penalty action against the driver is warranted in this case: the driver has 681 trips in 90 days with 2 disputes and 0 upheld, and the rider has 0 upheld disputes in the same window, so the route-dispute flag threshold of an already-upheld prior deviation is not met.

weaknesses: The GPS record F3 does show a genuine 4.84 km off-route segment between 09:06 and 09:13, and the trip as a whole covered 21.6 km against an optimal 16.6 km (F1) with duration 32.7 min vs 22 min estimated (F2); the rider will argue on RD-1 that any unexplained deviation breaches the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation, and F3 is the strongest fact against us.

Our justification is only partial under RD-4: there is no traffic incident at all (F12), so RD-4(a) fails and we must rely on the speed bands F10/F11, which under RD-4(b) are corroborative only and do not justify a re-route on their own; the chat record (F7, F8, F9) also contains no rider consent to the re-route as RD-5 requires, since the driver's statement that 'it rerouted me' was made only after the fact.

The rider's complaint that 'the meter came to 17 km' sits awkwardly beside the fixed-fare evidence F4/F6; if the adjudicator treats the ride as distance-sensitive, the 4.84 km in F3 becomes the base for a partial refund rather than zero.

events.body:
The trip was a RydeX fixed-quote job: the fare breakdown shows base $3.90 + distance $23.39 (for 16.6 km) + time $5.62 + platform $1.47 = $34.38, with waiting $0.00, no surge (1.0×) and no manual add-on [F4][F6][F5][FARE-1]. Billed distance (16.6 km) does not exceed the optimal route (16.6 km), so no distance overcharge reached the rider's bill [F4][RD-2].

On the route itself, the GPS record shows one genuine off-route segment 09:06–09:13 of 4.84 km where the optimal route covers 0.00 km, straying up to 1176 m off the optimal path, making 21.6 km actual vs 16.6 km optimal and 32.7 min vs 22 min estimated [F3][F1][F2][RD-1]. No exemption rescues it: the chat contains only pickup logistics at 08:49 — no driver route proposal before the segment and no rider agreement [F7][F8][RD-5]; no traffic incident was recorded on the route during the trip window [F12][RD-4]; and the driver's own statement "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me" confirms the change was made without prior agreement [F9][RD-5]. This is a RydeX non-metered trip with a fixed quoted fare, so RD-2's non-metered branch applies: the fare itself is not affected by excess mileage, and the only refundable element is any unpublished or non-qualifying add-on; the fare breakdown shows waiting $0.00 (F6) and no unpublished manual add-on beyond billed distance 16.6 km (F4) and published platform fee $1.47 (F6), while surge is 1.0× (F5).

The driver is nonetheless in breach of the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation on the 4.84 km unjustified segment, so the record should show a route-deviation violation even where the computed monetary refund under RD-2 is zero.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against my refund is F4: the billed distance (16.6 km) does not exceed the optimal route (16.6 km), and F6 shows the fare is a fixed quote (base $3.90 + distance $23.39 + time $5.62 + platform $1.47 = $34.38) with no excess-distance or unpublished line item — under RD-2's non-metered branch this drives the computed refund to $0 and an outcome of no_action, so my client's request to 'refund the extra distance' cannot be converted into a cash amount.

The driver's defence (F9, 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me') is supported by Ryde's own allowance that drivers may take the route their GPS calls fastest or most efficient; the traffic bands on AYE (40–49 km/h, F10) and CTE (30–39 km/h, F11) show some congestion on the corridors, and although RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt a segment, the judge may treat these as context for why the GPS rerouted.

The rider's complaint says 'the app estimated 17 km ... the meter came to 17 km', which conflicts with the system records F1/F4 (16.6 km optimal and 16.6 km billed); per the record-priority rule the rider's own numbers are unreliable and the judge may discount the complaint's framing, relying instead on F1/F3.
The rider's 90-day history shows 2 disputes, 0 upheld (F14), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of unsuccessful fare complaints.

The rider's demand to 'refund the extra distance' has no monetary basis: RD-2's refund formula only applies to metered RydeTAXI fares, and for a non-metered service such as RydeX the refundable amount for a distance complaint is zero, which maps to no_action.

The one off-route segment (09:06–09:13, 4.84 km added, up to 1176 m off the optimal route) generated no charge to the rider at all, since no unpublished surcharge, ERP/toll item or waiting fee appears on the bill and waiting was $0.00.

The rerouted segment is explained by a GPS re-route taken in dense traffic with no incidents: the optimal corridor's Ayer Rajah Expressway ran at speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) and the Central Expressway at band 4 (30–39 km/h) throughout the trip window, and Ryde permits the driver to follow the GPS to the fastest or most efficient route.

There is no unrecovered detour to refund because the driver did not collect any excess metered amount — no surge was applied (1.0×) and the fare breakdown contains no manual or unpublished add-on items.

No penalty action against the driver is warranted in this case: the driver has 681 trips in 90 days with 2 disputes and 0 upheld, and the rider has 0 upheld disputes in the same window, so the route-dispute flag threshold of an already-upheld prior deviation is not met.

weaknesses: The GPS record F3 does show a genuine 4.84 km off-route segment between 09:06 and 09:13, and the trip as a whole covered 21.6 km against an optimal 16.6 km (F1) with duration 32.7 min vs 22 min estimated (F2); the rider will argue on RD-1 that any unexplained deviation breaches the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation, and F3 is the strongest fact against us.

Our justification is only partial under RD-4: there is no traffic incident at all (F12), so RD-4(a) fails and we must rely on the speed bands F10/F11, which under RD-4(b) are corroborative only and do not justify a re-route on their own; the chat record (F7, F8, F9) also contains no rider consent to the re-route as RD-5 requires, since the driver's statement that 'it rerouted me' was made only after the fact.

Accepted that because this is a non-metered RydeX fare (F4, F6) the RD-2 per-km refund formula yields zero, so my client's cash demand cannot be granted; I therefore maintain only the RD-1 violation finding, which D2 does not rebut.

Agreed that the 4.84 km segment produced no separate charge — waiting is $0.00 and no unpublished manual add-on appears (F3, F6) — but the absence of a charge removes the refund, not the breach: RD-2 itself records the RD-1 violation where no exemption applies, and the driver's own statement (F9) confirms he rerouted without telling the rider.

This is the driver's weakest point: D4 concedes there is no incident at all (F12), and RD-4(a) requires an incident, so only the speed bands F10/F11 remain — RD-4(b) makes those corroborative only and expressly not sufficient for exemption in the MVP; RD-5 also fails because the chat (F7, F8) shows no route consent before the 09:06 segment start (F3).

Agreed on the money: no surge (F5) and no unpublished add-on (F6) means there is no detour amount to refund, so my requested outcome is already no_action on refund — D5 does not disturb the RD-1 finding that the 4.84 km segment (F3) was unexplained.

I do not contest this: the driver's record shows 681 trips, 2 disputes and 0 upheld (F15) and the rider's equally 0 upheld (F14), so RD-6's repeated-offender condition is not met and I request no flag_account against the driver.

The deviation itself is on the record (F3), but it is the wrong basis for money: the trip's only charge consequence is the quoted fare, and F6 shows the billed distance line of 16.6 km matches F4's optimal 16.6 km exactly, so no extra kilometre reached the rider's bill.

Conceded that no RD-5 consent exists (chat F7/F8 is pickup logistics only, F9 was said after the fact) and no RD-4(a) incident exists (F12); but the segment was still not a gratuitous detour, because the corridors were running slow — AYE band 5 at 40–49 km/h (F10) and CTE band 4 at 30–39 km/h (F11) over the exact trip window — and Ryde lets the driver follow the GPS to the fastest or most efficient route.
